title: Split "Lock Keys Status" widget into multiple ones so each of them can display an icon for one lock key
line: A new Num Lock Status widget can be enabled in the System Tray, so Caps Lock and Num Lock each get their own icon instead of one merged icon.
explanation: The Lock Keys Status widget tracks Caps Lock (and optionally Num Lock) in one System Tray item, and tray items are a single square icon. With both keys tracked and active it shows one combined "A1" icon, so you can't tell the two states apart at a glance; by default Num Lock isn't shown at all. The change adds a second widget, Num Lock Status (org.kde.plasma.numlockindicator), a metadata-only package that reuses the Lock Keys code through X-Plasma-RootPath (like Activity Pager and Application Dashboard); when loaded under that id it tracks only Num Lock, ignores the other modifiers and hides the Keys settings page.

commits.message:
applets/keyboardindicator: add a separate Num Lock Status widget

System Tray items only have room for one icon, so tracking both Caps
Lock and Num Lock merged them into one combined icon. Add a Num Lock
Status widget that reuses the Lock Keys code, so each key gets an icon.

BUG: 489824

media.caption: Caps Lock and Num Lock both on, default settings: only the Caps Lock icon, Num Lock state is not shown.
Same keys with Num Lock Status enabled: two separate icons, "A" and "1".
Lock Keys Status set to track both keys: one merged "A1" icon.
With the fix each key has its own icon and tooltip ("Num Lock Status — Num Lock activated").
System Tray settings, Entries filtered by "lock": only Lock Keys Status.
The new Num Lock Status entry, here switched to "Show when relevant".

reviews.text: Reusing keyboardindicator via X-Plasma-RootPath for a separate org.kde.plasma.numlockindicator widget is a clean, backwards-compatible way to give Caps Lock and Num Lock separate tray icons without breaking existing configurations. However, main.qml still instantiates the five sticky-modifier KeyState objects for Num Lock Status and does not guard them in toolTipSubText, so latched or locked modifiers (e.g. Shift via Sticky Keys) leak into Num Lock Status's tooltip and popup text.
changes: In applets/keyboardindicator/main.qml, skip instantiating altState, shiftState, controlState, metaState, and altGrState when isNumLockIndicator is true, and guard the modifier checks in toolTipSubText with !root.isNumLockIndicator (or null checks) so sticky-key modifier states never appear in Num Lock Status's tooltip or expanded popup.

Consider returning a Num Lock-specific inactive tooltip/placeholder message (e.g. "Num Lock deactivated") when isNumLockIndicator is true and Num Lock is off, instead of the generic "No lock keys activated".
